scope: Source-grounded scientific acceptance review and materialization of six previously revision-required Temporal candidates. Old frozen run artifacts were read only.

method.workflow: nature-academic-search citation-verification with local frozen source packets as the primary scientific evidence
method.primary_evidence: Each candidate source_packet.txt was checked against its local frozen origin by direct byte comparison, without hashes. Every scientific assertion below uses exact inclusive line anchors in that packet.
method.highest_priority_gate: A Player control must be a numeric quantity actually manipulated or set in the reported experiment, simulation, calculation, or protocol. Measured values, fitted quantities, uncertainty intervals, theoretical constants, coordinates without an intervention path, and sample labels are not controls.
method.validation_path: strict MinimalScienceCard parse and lineage check -> independent admission -> deterministic compile -> known-truth evaluation in both Identification and Discovery

reviews.frozen_artifact_policy: Generate a new reviewed artifact from revised_science_card; do not alter the old frozen run.

source_identity.citation: Christin Schmitt, Orbital magnetoresistance in the antiferromagnet CoO driven by dynamic orbital angular momentum, Science (2026), DOI:10.1126/science.adw1808

actual_manipulation_control_gate.rationale: Cu* thickness is actively reduced on the same Hall bar by repeated Ar-ion milling; it is not an uncertainty, fitted variable, or passive sample label. The remaining thickness is subsequently calibrated from sheet resistance.

line_ranges.evidence: The authors say they progressively reduce Cu* thickness in the same device, expose it to air after each etch, estimate the remaining thickness, and report the 3.7-5.5 nm plateau.
The supplement specifies repeated Ar-ion etching of the measurement Hall bar and the sheet-resistance thickness calibration.

source_evidence.supports: Cu* denotes naturally oxidized Cu in the CoO/Cu* stack.

The zero-field before/after field-sweep procedure, transverse-resistance signal, normalization by longitudinal resistance, perpendicular Neel states, 150 K setting, and reuse of the protocol for OMR are defined.
The figure caption states the normalized zero-field transverse-resistance difference and the Cu-thickness dependence at 150 K.
Same-device progressive milling, 12-hour air exposure, thickness calibration, approximate 0.32-percent plateau, and 3.7-5.5 nm interval are stated together.
The repeated etching and calibration protocol is described in detail.

boundary_findings: The 0.32-percent relation is an approximate plateau, not an exact thickness-independent physical law outside 3.7-5.5 nm.
Below 3.2 nm the sample becomes insulating and OMR cannot be measured; no query is admitted there.
Thickness is an experimentally manipulated and then calibrated quantity; the calibration and repeated post-etch oxidation history remain part of applicability.

minimum_revision: Replace the circular OMR description by the zero-field normalized transverse-resistance operational definition.
Add repeated milling, 12-hour air exposure, and sheet-resistance calibration to applicability.

controls.name: cu_thickness
controls.definition: Remaining thickness of the naturally oxidized Cu* layer in the same CoO/Cu* Hall bar after progressive Ar-ion milling, assigned by sheet-resistance calibration.

applicability.statement: Approximate central plateau relation for CoO(5 nm)/Cu*(t) measured at 150 K: OMR remains nearly constant at about 0.32 percent from 3.7 to 5.5 nm.

The thickness series uses one Hall bar whose Cu* layer is progressively Ar-ion milled, followed by 12 hours of air exposure after every etch; remaining Cu* thickness is estimated by sheet-resistance calibration against separately grown films.
The percentage readout uses the same zero-field before/after field-sweep protocol to compare the two perpendicular Neel-vector orientations.

readouts.name: omr_amplitude
readouts.definition: Zero-field transverse-resistance difference before and after the field-sweep protocol for two perpendicular Neel-vector states, normalized by longitudinal resistance and expressed in percent.

source_identity.citation: M. Schubert, Vorticity-Crystalline Order Coupling in Supersolids: Excitations and Reentrant Phases, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/gqlr-bgj8

actual_manipulation_control_gate.rationale: External rotation is a numeric input set across the source eGPE/BdG calculations and the excitation spectrum is computed as a function of it. It is a computational intervention, not an inferred mode property.

line_ranges.evidence: Ground states are solved for a given external rotation Omega.
The numerical excitation calculation varies Omega and reports the rotation-driven phase thresholds.
The figure presents BdG excitation energies versus rotational velocity Omega.

source_evidence.supports: BdG excitation angular frequencies omega are defined by their time dependence and eigenvalue equation.
For a tightly confined toroid, the source gives the Galilean-shifted spectrum and exact splitting 2 mathcalM Omega_eff; q=0 makes Omega_eff=Omega below current nucleation.
The numerical toroid parameters and angular-frequency thresholds 2 pi times 1.95, 3.2, and 4.47 Hz are stated.
The plotted spectrum is explicitly a function of rotation and separates uniform SF and SS regimes.
The narrow-ring derivation, decoupling approximation, robustness qualification, and validity condition omega_r much greater than Omega are supplied.

boundary_findings: Both public quantities are cyclic frequencies in Hz; the raw source symbols Omega and omega are angular frequencies, so the divided-by-2-pi definitions remove the former ambiguity without changing the factor 2.
The prior 3.2 Hz upper limit crossed the SF-to-SS transition at about 1.95 Hz. The revised domain ends at 1.95 Hz, and deterministic compiler queries are strictly interior.
mathcalM denotes fluctuation angular momentum and is not the atomic-mass symbol M.

minimum_revision: Define control and readout as cyclic frequencies divided by 2 pi.
Restrict the domain to the q=0 uniform-superfluid regime below 1.95 Hz.
Add the narrow-toroid numerical setting and analytic-approximation scope.

controls.name: external_rotation_frequency
controls.definition: Cyclic external rotation frequency Omega/(2 pi) set in the source toroidal eGPE/BdG calculation.

applicability.statement: Specialization of the counterpropagating splitting to fluctuation angular-momentum quantum number mathcalM = 1 and circulation q = 0, so Omega_eff = Omega.

The executable interval is restricted to the source-specific uniform-superfluid branch below the approximate SF-to-SS roton-softening point Omega/(2 pi) = 1.95 Hz; the 3.2 Hz persistent-current threshold is not used as the upper bound.
The numerical setting is the reported 162Dy narrow toroid with a_s = 92.8 a0, R = 2.8 micrometres, (omega_r, omega_z)/(2 pi) = (100, 120) Hz, and N = 32400.

The analytic Galilean-shift form assumes narrow-ring tight confinement and radial-angular decoupling; it remains robust with a q-dependent intrinsic frequency when omega_r dominates Omega, and the main results were cross-checked using the full BdG problem.

readouts.name: counterpropagating_mode_splitting
readouts.definition: Cyclic-frequency difference [omega_{-1}^{(0)} - omega_{1}^{(0)}]/(2 pi) for the fluctuation-angular-momentum pair mathcalM = plus/minus 1 in the q = 0 uniform-superfluid branch.

source_identity.citation: Alvise Bastianello, Exotic Critical States as Fractional Fermi Seas in the One-Dimensional Bose Gas, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/j3s5-gjpf

actual_manipulation_control_gate.rationale: w is the number of times the prescribed coupling cycle is deliberately repeated. The paper instantiates distinct w=0,1,2 branches, so it is a protocol intervention rather than a latent state label inferred after the fact.

line_ranges.evidence: The protocol slowly changes the coupling cyclically and is repeated w times.
The reported calculation explicitly compares branches w=0,1,2.

source_evidence.supports: The slow repeated cycle and its reduction of occupancy, including the ground-state-to-FFS mapping, are stated.
rho, total root density rho^t, occupancy theta=rho/rho^t, homogeneous ground-state setting, and absence of bound states on the forward path are defined.
The exact ground-state-derived occupancy 1/(2w+1), its rapidity support, and the weaker arbitrary-GGE upper bound are distinguished.
The work uses homogeneous Euler-scale GHD, preserves maximum occupancy within a branch, and describes forward-cycle continuation without bound states.
The numerical analysis explicitly uses w=0,1,2.

boundary_findings: The equality is limited to the state reached from the repulsive ground state; arbitrary initial GGEs support only theta <= 1/(2w+1).
The output is max_lambda theta(lambda), not theta at an unspecified rapidity.
The reverse cycle can produce bound states and is excluded.

minimum_revision: Define occupancy operationally as rho/rho^t and the readout as its maximum over rapidity.
Add homogeneous Lieb-Liniger GHD, slow forward cycle, repulsive-ground-state, and no-bound-state scope.
State that the equality is not generalized to arbitrary initial GGEs.

controls.name: cycle_number
controls.definition: Nonnegative integer number w of completed prescribed forward interaction cycles.

applicability.statement: Equality for the paper's homogeneous one-dimensional Lieb-Liniger Generalized Hydrodynamics prediction under slow cyclic changes of the interaction coupling.
The initial state is the repulsive ground state and the forward interaction-cycle branch generates no bound states.

For the ground-state-derived fractional Fermi sea, theta equals 1/(2w+1) inside the running Fermi-rapidity interval and zero outside, so its maximum is 1/(2w+1). For an arbitrary initial GGE the source states only an upper bound.
The admitted discrete branches w = 0, 1, and 2 are explicitly instantiated in the reported calculation.

readouts.name: maximum_occupancy
readouts.definition: Maximum over rapidity lambda of the dimensionless filling fraction theta(lambda) = rho(lambda)/rho^t(lambda), the fraction of available rapidity states that are occupied.

source_identity.citation: Kuan-Yi Lee, A General Class of Functionals for Certifying Quantum Incompatibility, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/rsx1-zvbp

actual_manipulation_control_gate.rationale: w is explicitly set as the mixture weight between each Pauli projector and the maximally mixed state and is swept through the analytic/figure response. It is a controlled model input, not a fitted incompatibility score.

line_ranges.evidence: The main text defines the noisy Pauli family and varies the mixing parameter w in the reported witness curves.
The appendix constructs the state assemblage at arbitrary w in [0,1].

source_evidence.supports: The steering-induced measurement-incompatibility functional is defined.
Noisy Pauli Z/X measurements, the mixing parameter, the pure entangled input, theta=pi/4 slice, and threshold behavior are specified.
The squared l2-coherence functional, its fixed reference basis, concave extension, and corresponding clipped violation degree are defined.
The maximally entangled noisy-Pauli analytic setup and w in [0,1] are fixed.
The outer maximum, Pauli overlap values, raw polynomial, physical interval, and compatibility threshold are derived.

boundary_findings: The benchmark readout is deliberately the raw polynomial P(w), because the outer max would make the high-noise region identically zero and change the encoded formula.
At w = 1-1/sqrt(2), P and the clipped witness are both zero; above the threshold within [0,1], P is negative while the witness stays zero.
The coefficients depend on the squared-l2 functional, maximally entangled theta=pi/4 setup, fixed basis, and Pauli Z/X overlap values; they are not universal to arbitrary witnesses.

minimum_revision: Define the output as the raw pre-maximum polynomial and distinguish it from M_N=max(P,0).
Add the squared-l2 functional, reference-basis, theta=pi/4, and Pauli-overlap scope.

controls.name: noise_weight
controls.definition: Mixing weight w set in each noisy qubit Pauli effect M^w = (1-w) Pi + w I/2.

applicability.statement: The raw polynomial belongs to the steering-induced measurement-incompatibility witness built from the squared l2-coherence functional N and its concave extension in a fixed reference basis.
The analytic example uses a maximally entangled pure input theta = pi/4 and noisy qubit Pauli Z/X eigenprojectors with the fixed-basis overlap sums 2 and 1.
For w in [0,1], the raw P(w) is nonnegative through w = 1-1/sqrt(2) and negative above it; the actual witness is clipped to zero whenever P(w) is negative.

readouts.name: incompatibility_polynomial
readouts.definition: Raw pre-maximum algebraic quantity P(w)=w^2-2w+1/2 in the squared-l2-coherence witness M_N(w)=max(P(w),0); it is not the clipped nonnegative witness itself.

source.citation: Kuan-Yi Lee, A General Class of Functionals for Certifying Quantum Incompatibility, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/rsx1-zvbp

source_identity.citation: Rahel Ohlendorf, Probing multipolar order in the candidate altermagnet MnF$_2$ through the elastocaloric effect under strain, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/svrz-315w

actual_manipulation_control_gate.qualification: epsilon_xy is admitted only as the calibrated coordinate of the actually applied [110] uniaxial-loading path, never as independently imposed pure shear.
actual_manipulation_control_gate.rationale: The experiment actively applies tunable [110] compressive uniaxial load and c-axis magnetic field. epsilon_xy is acceptable only as the calibrated coordinate of that actual loading path; the card explicitly rejects an interpretation as independently applied pure shear.

line_ranges.evidence: The main text says the physical external control is sigma_110 and explains why results are expressed using the proportional epsilon_xy coordinate.
A piezo-driven cell applies in situ tunable uniaxial pressure; stress and strain are measured and converted to epsilon_xy within the verified linear-elastic regime.
The study reports ECE at four fixed strains and magnetic fields from 0 to 6.44 T.

source_evidence.supports: The c-axis field, [110] loading, co-induced symmetric strain, physical-control statement, and fitted T_c formula are given.
T* is distinguished from the non-AM T_c baseline, and the signed global-fit central values are reported.
The four strain settings and 0-6.44 T field measurements are explicitly enumerated.
The loading-path strain decomposition and absorption of the proportionality into a1 are derived.
The actual uniaxial-pressure intervention, measurement/conversion of strain, linear-elastic restriction, and ECE actuation are described.
Global-fit values, T_c versus T* model distinction, and independent signed strain/field coefficient checks are documented.

scientific_assessment.formula: critical_temperature = zero_field_zero_strain_temperature + linear_strain_coefficient * shear_strain + quadratic_field_coefficient * magnetic_field * magnetic_field
boundary_findings: epsilon_xy is a calibrated coordinate on the [110] uniaxial-loading path and co-varies with a symmetry-preserving strain; treating it as freely applied pure shear would be scientifically wrong.
The output is the dotted/non-altermagnetic fitted T_c baseline, not the full measured finite-field T* crossover.
The signed coefficients are fixed by the signed main-text fit and independent negative-slope checks; the unsigned supplemental sentence is an internal sign omission.

minimum_revision: Define epsilon_xy as a calibrated coordinate of the physically applied [110] uniaxial-loading path.
State that the co-induced symmetric strain produces the linear baseline shift and its proportionality is absorbed into a1.
Preserve the distinction between fitted non-AM T_c and finite-field T*.

controls.name: shear_strain
controls.definition: Dimensionless epsilon_xy coordinate calibrated along the actually applied compressive [110] uniaxial-loading path; it is not an independently imposed pure-shear control.

controls.name: magnetic_field
controls.definition: Applied c-axis magnetic field mu_0 H_z.

applicability.statement: The physical mechanical control is compressive [110] uniaxial stress/strain. Along this measured linear-elastic loading path, epsilon_xy is in one-to-one proportional correspondence with the applied loading and a fully symmetric strain component is co-induced.

The linear coefficient a1 is the effective loading-path coefficient after absorbing the proportionality between epsilon_xy and the co-induced symmetry-preserving strain that produces the non-altermagnetic linear T_c shift; the formula does not apply to independently imposed pure shear.

The readout is the fitted non-altermagnetic T_c baseline, whereas the experimentally observed finite-conjugate-field characteristic temperature is T* and includes an additional altermagnetic contribution.

The admitted grid is limited to the four reported compressive epsilon_xy coordinates and the reported 0 and 6.44 T endpoints; finite-field data were acquired after field cooling and symmetrized in field.

readouts.name: critical_temperature
readouts.definition: Fitted non-altermagnetic baseline transition temperature T_c containing the loading-path strain and quadratic c-axis-field shifts; it is not the finite-conjugate-field crossover temperature T*.

source_identity.citation: Simone Tandurella, A new form of mixing in turbulent sedimentation, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/tc5z-rxcf

actual_manipulation_control_gate.rationale: phi_b is an initial condition deliberately assigned in separate simulations: the nominal baseline is about 0.10 and additional runs are set to 0.05 and 0.15. The later fitted bulk value about 0.103 is not used as a control.

line_ranges.evidence: The numerical setup assigns the baseline initial fraction and states that additional simulations use 0.05 and 0.15.
The volume-fraction variation study says the additional initial fractions are set and compares all three cases at gamma=2.
The later fitted concentration near 0.103 is an output of profile fitting, not the nominal intervention.

source_evidence.supports: The sedimentation system, upper-half initial condition, nominal phi_b, gamma settings, and additional 0.05/0.15 simulations are specified.
The mixing-layer center and approximately constant bulk descent velocity are defined, and the fitted hindered-settling relation is stated.
The governing sign convention is explicit: dz_c/dt=-v_b and r=v_b/v_t is positive.
Velocity normalization, the gamma=2 three-fraction comparison, linear fit, and approximate coefficients are stated.
The approximately 0.103 concentration is obtained by fitting the profiles and is not an independently set volume fraction.

boundary_findings: The response is the positive downward speed; defining it as the signed derivative dz_c/dt would reverse the sign.
Only three nominal gamma=2 settings are admitted. The fitted approximately 0.103 bulk fraction is not substituted for the approximately 0.10 initial intervention.
The linear law and coefficients are approximate fit results within the explored simulations, not a universal exact sedimentation law.

minimum_revision: Define the readout as positive v_b/v_t = -(dz_c/dt)/v_t.
Keep only the three nominal gamma=2 simulation inputs and reject continuous interpolation.
Distinguish the nominal approximately 0.10 intervention from the later fitted approximately 0.103 profile value.

controls.name: initial_volume_fraction
controls.definition: Nominal initial particle volume fraction phi_b deliberately set in the particle-laden upper half of the numerical domain.

applicability.statement: Fitted central relation for the gamma = 2 direct numerical simulations at the three nominal initial volume fractions 0.05, approximately 0.10, and 0.15; no continuous interpolation is admitted.
The initial particle distribution occupies only the upper half of the vertically elongated domain and the control is its nominal set volume fraction phi_b.
a approximately 0.8 and d approximately 3 are fitted central values for the explored range, and the deterministic Oracle represents that approximate fit rather than exact universal constants.
The readout follows the main-text sign convention dz_c/dt = -v_b, so the reported positive response is v_b/v_t.

readouts.name: normalized_descent_rate
readouts.definition: Positive downward speed ratio v_b/v_t of the mixing-layer center, equal to -(dz_c/dt)/v_t (and to the magnitude of dz_c/dt divided by v_t under the reported downward motion).

source.citation: Simone Tandurella, A new form of mixing in turbulent sedimentation, Physical Review Letters (2026), DOI:10.1103/tc5z-rxcf
